# Capabilities in delfin/agent/ that the PRODUCT does not reach.
#
# Written by tests/test_every_capability_has_a_caller.py, which refuses a
# name that is not in here. Columns: tier, name, where it is defined.
#
# tier "nowhere"   -- nothing in delfin/ or tests/ names it at all. Dead
#                     code, or a capability that was never connected.
# tier "test-only" -- only the suite reaches it. The capability exists and
#                     is proven, and nothing in the running product uses
#                     it.
#
# A name LEAVES this list by being connected or deleted, and the test then
# requires the list to be shortened: the count only goes down. Adding a
# line is a deliberate act and belongs in a pull request of its own, with
# the reason.
#
# Measured 2026-11-20, by the functions in that test file, so the list
# and the check cannot compute it differently.
# _bypass_failure_asks STAYS, measured 2026-11-22. The mount it was
# written for -- extending the classifier's on_error at
# _classifier_second_opinion so a failure on the high-risk class asks even
# for workspace work -- would change no outcome: for every action the
# predicate calls high-risk, _leaves_workspace already returns True one
# line earlier, so on_error is already "ask" (or "refuse" with nobody to
# ask). Measured over 15 bash commands spanning every branch of the
# pattern, remote_trigger, push_notification, a session message and all
# four _BYPASS_HIGH_RISK_WRITE_NAMES inside the workspace -- including the
# .gitconfig case the mount was proposed for -- against the control that
# routine actions (python3 build.py, cp, ls, git status, git commit, an
# ordinary write) have leaves False. So the guarantee is delivered by
# _leaves_workspace plus the deny list, the push gate and the egress scan,
# which refuse several of them before any classifier is consulted.
# Its job here is to PIN that: test_the_high_risk_class_is_inside_what_
# leaves_the_workspace fails if _leaves_workspace ever stops asking for one
# of them. Deleting it would remove the only explicit statement of the
# class; mounting it would add a call that cannot change an answer.
test-only	_bypass_failure_asks	delfin/agent/api_client.py:14120
# _disabled_keyring_factory stays test-only, measured 2026-11-22: the
# conftest autouse fixture swaps it in (tests/conftest.py:1599) so no test
# touches the real keyring, and _keyring_factory is only ever bound to
# _default_keyring_factory (delfin/agent/credentials.py:400) -- no
# production path disables the keyring. Mounting one would be a new
# capability; what would decide a delete is a product need to run
# keyless, which does not exist.
test-only	_disabled_keyring_factory	delfin/agent/credentials.py:360
# category_names STAYS, and the reason is the measure's own weak spot: this
# test counts any mention of a name, so `from .compaction_quality import
# category_names` in the funnel module would close the row without anything
# in the product ever calling it. It would read as reached and be no more
# reached than before. The product gets the seven category names from the
# report's own keys (record_compaction writes them as it receives them), so
# there is nothing here for a product caller to want. Mounting it needs a
# consumer that iterates the categories in a fixed order -- a renderer or
# the long-run metric -- which is its own change, not a line in an import.
test-only	category_names	delfin/agent/compaction_quality.py:169
test-only	for_files	delfin/agent/verify_recipe.py:327
test-only	is_safe	delfin/agent/readonly_pipeline.py:371
# _locator_value (cited_retrieval.py:218) DELETED 2026-11-22: zero callers
# anywhere, including its own module -- check_answer_citations reads the
# locator dicts from locator_for directly (cited_retrieval.py:287-291) and
# never normalises to (kind, value). The whole cited_retrieval module has
# no product import yet; the deletion needs no second answer because the
# job it did is inline dict access in its own module.
# bwrap_substitution: measured 2026-11-22 (wave 37, group rr1). Neither mounting
# nor deleting is right yet. The wiring contract is tests/test_shared_tmp_wiring.py,
# xfail(strict) with reason "operator wiring pending": the swap belongs in
# api_client._bash_isolation_argv (delfin/agent/api_client.py:31275), which still
# mounts --tmpfs /tmp. api_client.py is forbidden to this group (rule 13), so the
# mount cannot be made here; deleting would orphan that contract. Decides it: the
# operator wiring commit replacing --tmpfs /tmp with the session-dir bind.
# NOT removed 2026-11-22 (wave 36 c1, re-measured): there are two
# category vocabularies for one job. The product's compaction record
# carries its loss under the key ``lost`` in working_state's four
# categories (compaction_log.LOSS_CATEGORIES: denials, tests, files,
# instructions); category_names() is a second, broader keep-list list
# (goal, instruction, constraints, refusals, decisions, waits, tests)
# whose only reader would be a consumer of quality_report, which is
# itself unmounted one row below. Reporting a metric in this vocabulary
# would make five of its seven categories None forever, so the mount
# attempted here was withdrawn; the loss metric reports in the writer's
# vocabulary instead. Deciding which of the two lists the product should
# keep is a design decision, not a repair.
# check_ordering STAYS (measured 2026-11-22, wave 37 rr2): nothing in the
# product inspects a recorded head -- the engine turn (engine.py:3084)
# composes via compose_sections, joins (_held_system_prompt) and sends;
# the layer order is guaranteed at the source by construction
# (prompt_loader.py:2050 "the composition order IS the layer order"), so a
# product-composed head cannot violate it. The check is the suite/human
# measurement layer over recorded rows (as the adversarial test does:
# record the real engine rows, call the check from the test). Mounting it
# in the engine turn would be a tautological new surface (rule 12); the
# question that decides it is whether the product should surface an
# ordering violation to a person -- a design decision, not a repair.
# enforce_quota: measured 2026-11-22 (wave 37, group rr1). Neither mounting nor
# deleting is right yet. Zero product callers: the product's own session scratch
# (api_client._session_scratch_dir, delfin/agent/api_client.py:29532) never
# calls shared_tmp at all, and no cleanup path in delfin/ names this function.
# Deleting would orphan the quota pin tests (tests/test_shared_tmp_cleanup.py);
# mounting would need a product cleanup tick that does not exist (new surface,
# rule 12). Decides it: wiring the session-end cleanup to enforce_quota, or an
# operator decision that the product never quotas scratch.
# for_files (verify_recipe.py:327) KEPT as test-only 2026-11-22, measured:
# zero product callers. The product consumers of verify_recipe hold a
# recipe but never a changed-file list -- prompt_loader.py:1002-1003 calls
# discover+render, evidence.py:203 calls discover -- so narrowing a recipe
# to changed files (for_files) is unreachable by construction today.
# Deciding WHICH consumer would gain a changed-file list is a design
# decision, not a repair; wiring one arbitrarily would mount a call on a
# path that runs but does not need it. Revisit if a consumer starts
# holding both a recipe and a diff.
# hostile_reach STAYS (measured 2026-11-22, wave 37 rr2): the only rows in
# a product-composed head that carry data (briefing, lessons, decomposition,
# chemistry, repo_map -- prompt_loader.py:2234-2264) are all LAYER_VOLATILE,
# which hostile_reach exempts (layer >= 2); the layer 0/1 rows are trusted
# addendum files and fixed route text. Product rows therefore cannot trip
# the check by construction -- it guards a future layer-assignment
# regression that would reclassify data into the cacheable head. Mounting
# it in the engine turn would be a per-turn tautology / new surface
# (rule 12); the deciding question is whether the product should enforce
# the invariant per turn -- a design decision, not a repair.
# NOT removed 2026-11-22 (wave 36 r4, then re-measured at the GATE, not
# at the predicate): is_safe is not redundant, but the predicate numbers
# r4 reported overstate what the product does, and both measurements are
# recorded here because the difference between them is the lesson.
#
# At the predicate (KitToolPermissions.matches_bash_auto_allow,
# api_client.py:11109), default mode: 8 commands are auto-allowed that
# is_safe refuses -- ls > f, ls 3>f, ls >&f, ls &>f, cat <>f,
# sort --out=f x, sort --compress-program=sh x, git reflog expire --all.
#
# At the gate (_run_permission_gate, the entry a bash call really takes,
# which consults the predicate only after the deny list, the secret scan,
# the approval guard, the irreversibility rule and unrestorable.refusal):
# git reflog expire --expire=now --all ASKS, and echo x >
# ~/.ssh/authorized_keys is refused outright (secret-deny). What runs
# unasked is the redirect family inside the workspace -- which is
# deliberate policy, documented in matches_bash_auto_allow itself, and
# confined by the cage -- plus two classes that are not:
#   * a redirect whose TARGET is outside the workspace
#     (echo x > ~/.bashrc, ls > /tmp/elsewhere.txt, ls > ../escape.txt:
#     RUN, no question; _changes_outside_the_workspace does not read
#     redirection targets at all),
#   * a flag that runs a program (sort --compress-program=sh x and the
#     space form: RUN, no question).
# Controls at the gate: ls -la, git status, cat f, grep x f, grep -r,
# python3 --version, pytest all RUN; rm -rf f and git push --force are
# refused by deny-pattern; curl -T asks.
#
# So a blanket veto on is_safe would be wrong: at the predicate it also
# refuses grep -r, sed -n, awk, find, python3 --version, pytest, mkdir
# and touch, which the list grants on purpose. The repair is the two
# classes above, in api_client.py, which the self-modification guard
# refuses to an unattended session. Kept until that attended change
# lands; deleting the row would discard a judgement the gate still needs.
# map_to_host: measured 2026-11-22 (wave 37, group rr1). Neither mounting nor
# deleting is right yet. The wiring contract is tests/test_shared_tmp_wiring.py,
# xfail(strict): the mapping belongs in api_client._execute_read_file
# (delfin/agent/api_client.py:18215) BEFORE the read gate, so /tmp/... resolves
# to the session dir. api_client.py is forbidden to this group (rule 13); deleting
# would orphan the contract and the mapping rules pinned by tests/test_shared_tmp.py.
# Decides it: the operator wiring commit in _execute_read_file.
# quality_report STAYS (measured 2026-11-22, wave 37 rr2): the product's
# compaction-loss answer is compare_loss (compaction_log.py:119), mounted in
# two live places (record_compaction at compaction_log.py:78, in_turn at
# in_turn_compaction.py:307), and it reports in working_state's four
# categories (denials, tests, files, instructions). quality_report is a
# second, broader seven-category keep-list with no writer on the product
# path -- the same two-vocabularies finding as the category_names row above
# (that row's reason lives on the wave-36-c1 branch swarm/w36-c1-l1-t2,
# not yet merged). Wave 36 c1 already attempted and withdrew the mount:
# in this vocabulary five of the seven categories would read as forever
# missing, so the loss metric reports in the writer's vocabulary instead.
# Deciding which vocabulary the product keeps is a design decision, not a
# repair.
# NOT removed 2026-11-22 (wave 36 r4): the product's per-turn reset is
# begin_figure_turn (office.py:6070, driven by engine.py:3482), which opens
# a NEW token'd scope and pops only that token -- it cannot clear an
# existing scope on demand, and eviction (office.py:6051) only trims stale
# scopes. No product path is equivalent to an explicit clear; the office
# tool runs are the consumers and keep needing it between turns.
test-only	reset_figure_ledger	delfin/agent/office.py:6098
test-only	role_tool_surface_report	delfin/agent/api_client.py:12107

# Rows added 2026-11-25 by the widening of the census to delfin/tools/.
# Measured on the tree BEFORE that widening: delfin/tools/ held 591
# module-level callables the census had never looked at, 5 unreached. Two of
# those five are gone -- write_co2_scan_opi_input is mounted on the
# co2_coordinator_opi step (tests/test_co2_step_writes_both_classic_inputs.py)
# and _kind_name was deleted (delfin/tools/scaffold.py): the product never
# infers a kind from a name, because new-adapter takes --kind as an argparse
# choices with default "program" (delfin/agent/cli_new_adapter.py:29-31) and
# build_scaffold refuses anything outside _KINDS (scaffold.py:159). Three stay.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# normalise_esd_inp STAYS, and it carries a finding rather than an excuse.
# It is the only caller of the five ESD block normalisers (_normalise_tddft_
# block, _normalise_esd_block, _normalise_geom_block, _normalise_basis_block,
# _normalise_output_block, esd_opi.py:48,74,99,108,120), and the ESD parity
# test does not use it: test_esd_input_parity normalises with
# delfin.tools.co2_coordinator_opi.normalise_inp (imported at
# tests/test_opi_esd_parity.py:47, used at :280-281), which parses no
# %tddft / %esd / %basis / %output block at all.
# Measured 2026-11-25 on the two texts differing ONLY in `%tddft nroots 5`
# vs `6`, written in the multi-line block form the writers emit, with each
# normaliser's own output compared block by block:
#   co2_coordinator_opi.normalise_inp  blocks {'pal'}         -> equal, blind
#   esd_opi.normalise_esd_inp          blocks {'pal','tddft'} -> differs
#   ({'tddft': {'nroots': 5}} vs {'tddft': {'nroots': 6}})
# So the parity test, whose module docstring says it proves the OPI inputs
# equivalent "over the repo's CONTROL matrix", cannot see a difference inside
# those blocks. The mount is one line (swap the normaliser at
# tests/test_opi_esd_parity.py:280-281) and was deliberately NOT taken here:
# it changes what the parity test asserts instead of adding a product caller,
# the file is behind pytest.importorskip("opi") so a change to it cannot be
# shown red-then-green on a host without OPI, and it can turn red on real
# historic differences nobody has read yet. Whoever next runs the OPI job
# decides it.
nowhere	normalise_esd_inp	delfin/tools/esd_opi.py:131
# esd_inputs_equivalent is the other half of the same pair and stays for a
# different reason: a parity comparator has no product caller by nature. The
# product writes an ESD input through the classic driver
# (delfin/esd_input_generator.py, reached from cli.py) and never compares two
# inputs at runtime -- the parity proof IS the suite. Its tier is therefore
# correct, and note that the row above is what makes this one weaker than it
# looks: the comparator runs, on normalised inputs that drop the ESD blocks.
test-only	esd_inputs_equivalent	delfin/tools/esd_opi.py:181
# validate_relspin STAYS: mounting it would change no answer. The live path
# (OrcaRelSpinOpiAdapter.execute -> run_rel_sp/run_zfs/run_soc_tddft ->
# build_*_input) already runs every check it performs -- validate_method,
# _check_mult_triplet, _basis_check_error, the ZFS singlet refusal
# (orca_relspin_opi.py:606-611) and the SOC-TDDFT nroots refusal (733-737) --
# and each has a test that asserts the refusal (tests/test_opi_orca_relspin.py
# :245, 253, 261, 305, 314, 345). Mounting it as the adapter's validate_params
# hook (called at _runner.py:59, before the work dir exists) would therefore
# only refuse the same calls earlier, and would do so WEAKER: its elements
# default of None retires the electron-count parity branch of
# _check_mult_triplet, and it takes no extra_keywords, so a keyword the live
# builders validate would pass a pre-flight that the run itself refuses.
# Deleting it is not right either: it is the only callable that states all the
# relspin rules in one place, and 17 test call sites exercise it directly.
test-only	validate_relspin	delfin/tools/adapters/orca_relspin_opi.py:220
